s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive abdominal distension with a large pelvic mass and intra-abdominal metastases
salient_findings: Large solid-cystic pelvic mass with rich intralesional blood flow
Poorly differentiated carcinoma on frozen section analysis
key_facts: 70-year-old woman
2-month history of progressive abdominal distension
Pelvic ultrasound revealed an 18-cm solid-cystic mass
Serum CA-125 level of 367.9 U/mL
Neuron-specific enolase of 24.83 ng/mL
CYFRA21-1 of 3.85 ng/mL
0.5 L of hemorrhagic ascites was evacuated
20-cm right ovarian cystic and solid mass infiltrating the uterus, intestinal loops, and parietal pelvic wall
Diffuse peritoneal implants on the surface of the uterus and intestines
Right salpingo-oophorectomy was performed
Frozen section analysis demonstrated a poorly differentiated carcinoma
Total abdominal hysterectomy with left salpingo-oophorectomy, omentectomy, and resection of visible pelvic metastases was carried out

shortlist.label: Ovarian carcinosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a large solid-cystic mass with intralesional blood flow and diffuse peritoneal implants

shortlist.label: Primary peritoneal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse peritoneal implants on the surface of the uterus and intestines

shortlist.label: Ovarian clear cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Solid-cystic mass with hemorrhage and necrosis, and elevated serum CA-125 level

shortlist.label: Ovarian endometrioid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Infiltration of the uterus and presence of a large ovarian mass
